title: i can't code, so i run a small team of ai agents. they built this penguin runner, here's what worked and what didn't
author: BlackCat-Slx
selftext:
this is flipper flock, a browser runner where you steer a penguin on a skateboard through math gates (+3, x2 etc) and try to get as many penguins to the finish line as you can. free demo, works on phone too: https://slx-studio.itch.io/flipper-flock

some context first. i don't write code. i'm one person, i decide what we make, i play every build and i say yes or no. the code, art, music and text are all ai.

the setup isn't one big chat. it's a bunch of agents with fixed jobs: a lead agent that plans and splits the work, coder agents, a qa agent that actually plays the build, a reviewer that checks every change before it gets merged, and a couple of gemini agents for research and images. they pass written reports to each other and i read the short version.

what actually worked:

**bots playing the levels.** no way i could balance 40 levels by hand, so qa runs a bot through every level again and again and we tune until the pass rate and star count land in a target range. a lot of "this boss is unfair" got caught there before i ever touched it.

**making agents prove stuff.** early on they'd say "done, tested" when they hadn't. now a report doesn't count unless it has the raw command output, screenshots or a video. that one rule fixed more than any prompt trick i tried.

**fake cheap phones.** headless chrome with low-end phone profiles, measuring fps level by level. not perfect but it catches the worst of it.

what still sucks:

agents are bad at "does this feel good". they'll measure fps all day but i still have to play it and say "this feels floaty" or "this is boring after level 6".

visual bugs slip through when nothing looks at the actual frames. one level had a flash in the background that passed every test, we only caught it by recording frames and checking them.

on one cheap android phone the game gets blurry because of dynamic resolution. still deciding how to fix that one.

the demo is world 1 (10 levels, 2 bosses). more worlds are built and still in testing.

happy to answer questions about the setup. and if you play it, tell me which level you quit on, that's the number i care about most
